kgb.e: From Russian КГБ (KGB), acronym of Комите́т госуда́рственной безопа́сности (Komitét gosudárstvennoj bezopásnosti, “State Security Committee”).

d.g: Any of several types of public meeting in a Botswana village, especially one involving a gathering of tribal elders.
d.x: Speaking at the Mochudi main kgotla after the graduation of at least 1 281 initiates, Kgafela said though there were few challenges, the exercise had been successful.

kgosi.e: Etymology tree Proto-Bantu *nkócì Tswana kgosibor. English kgosi Borrowed from Tswana kgosi (“chief, chieftain; king”), from Proto-Bantu *nkócì (“lion”). Doublet of inkosi.

d.g: A district in south-west Botswana, which includes much of the Kalahari Desert.
A member of a Tswana people chiefly living in the Kalahari Desert.

Kgalagadi.e: Etymology tree Tswana kgala Tswana -gadi Tswana Kgalagadiubor. English Kgalagadi Unadapted borrowing from Tswana Kgalagadi (literally “a large, dry area”), from kgala (“become dry”) + -gadi (“large”). Doublet of Kalahari.
